chunks: Zur'ah narrated from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about the divorce of a boy who has not reached puberty and his dowry. He said: If he divorces for the sake of the Sunnah and places the dowry in its proper place and fulfills its right, there is no harm, and it is valid. This has been defined as ten years and above, according to what we have cited in our book, Al-Kabir.

key_terms.الْكِتَابِ الْكَبِيرِ: The Major Book (referring to Al-Kabir by Al-Shaykh Al-Tusi)
key_terms.لِلسُّنَّةِ: For the sake of the Sunnah / according to tradition

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the divorce of a boy who has not yet reached puberty?
ai.summary: This hadith from *al-Istibsar* clarifies that a pre-pubescent boy's divorce is legally valid (*jā'iz*) provided he follows the Sunnah and correctly allocates his dowry (*sadaqah*) from his own wealth. It establishes ten years as the age threshold for this capacity, a ruling elaborated upon in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *al-Kabir*, reflecting the Shia juristic view that financial and marital agency begins before full physical maturity. This underscores the principle that the minor’s guardian or the minor himself, if possessing sufficient discernment, can execute valid marital contracts and divorces.
